answer: The glacier check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. One enclave yields one identity, which means 882 clones would need 552 physical devices plus the garden attestation each must still earn by work. Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries an atlas quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. That is 39 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
